subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency/Throughput AB test follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@globex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency/Throughput AB test follow-up

Hi Aaron — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary from call:
- Globex is running a production inference pipeline for chat summarization (~8k seq during peak).
- You’re interested in latency/throughput head-to-head vs your current hyperscaler endpoints and an apples-to-apples Redwood run.
- Key metrics for you: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec sustained, and cost per 1M tokens.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) You share baseline metrics (p95/p99, tokens/sec) and any existing test configs — you mentioned a CSV export today.
2) We’ll run an A/B test with the same prompt mix and sequence lengths you use (we suggest 2k/4k/8k buckets).
3) Redwood will produce p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec (aggregated and by seq-length), plus a short runbook describing how to reproduce.

Can you send the baseline export and give us temporary access to your test project (or share an endpoint + keys) so we can mirror the test?

Attachments: none on my side yet — Rafael and Markus will own the test plan and results.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0138
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency/Throughput AB test follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great recap. Attaching our baseline export as requested (globex_baseline_metrics.csv). A few clarifications: 

- The production workload is a mix of short chat turns (avg ~120 tokens) and longer summarization jobs (up to 8k tokens); we see ~35% of traffic in the long bucket during nightly batch runs.
- Hyperscaler current baseline (from our monitoring) is roughly: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~480ms for the chat endpoint; sustained throughput ~3.2k tokens/sec when batched.
- We can create a short-lived test key for you against our staging project (we'll provision it tomorrow).

Please treat the baseline CSV as internal. Let me know what specific payload format you want and which sequence-length buckets you plan to run.

Aaron Liu
Senior Platform Engineer, Globex Corp
aaron.liu@globex.com
Attached: globex_baseline_metrics.csv
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@globex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency/Throughput AB test follow-up

Hi Aaron — I pulled the baseline and sketched an AB test plan (attached: redwood_abtest_plan_v1.pdf). High-level config: 

- Test duration: 2 hours for each arm (Hyperscaler / Redwood), repeated 3x across different time windows.
- Load profile: 70% chat-like (<=256 tokens), 20% mid (2k tokens), 10% long (8k tokens).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, percent timeouts, and cost estimation.
- Deterministic prompt set: we'll use your sample corpus you sent over (we will not store inputs beyond test duration).

Next asks from us: 
1) Can you grant a staging key or allow our test runner IPs (I’ll provide a small list)?
2) Please confirm the exact payload size and any rate limits we should respect.

I attached the plan for your review. Once we have access we’ll provision the test runners and share a reproducibility note.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@globex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency/Throughput AB test follow-up

Thanks Rafael — plan looks good. We created a staging key and a Hyperscaler test bundle (ID HC-9876) and attached the config (hyperscaler_test_config.json). For transparency, here are the observed baseline numbers from the Hyperscaler run: p95 = 220ms, p99 = 480ms, sustained tokens/sec = 3.2k.

We’ll whitelist these IPs for the test runner and will rotate the key after the test window. I’ve also opened a Jira ticket for tracking: https://hyperscalercloud.atlassian.net/browse/HC-1234.

Two quick questions:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood’s run will enable prefix KV caching for the long 8k sequences during the test? That was a call-out earlier and matters for p99.
- Any expectation on cost delta for 1M tokens so we can model procurement impact?

Aaron
Senior Platform Engineer, Globex Corp
Attached: hyperscaler_test_config.json
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@globex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: Latency/Throughput AB test follow-up

Hi Aaron — quick status and preliminary results from the first AB runs (attached CSV + charts). Short summary: 

Prelim Redwood (avg across windows):
- p95 = 180ms
- p99 = 420ms
- sustained tokens/sec = 3.8k
- Observed better long-sequence handling when KV/prefix caching enabled (we ran one set with caching on, one without).

Hyperscaler baseline you shared (for reference):
- p95 = 220ms
- p99 = 480ms
- sustained tokens/sec = 3.2k

Notes / next steps:
1) Results look favorable for Redwood on raw latency and throughput. We still want to run the full 3x windowed test to confirm stability and p99 tail behavior under longer run durations.
2) Rafael will produce a reproducibility runbook and a cost model (1M token delta) by Friday; I’ll include a short chart showing cost vs latency tradeoffs.
3) Aaron — can you introduce the procurement contact (or confirm the procurement cadence) so we can scope reserved capacity pricing if you decide to move forward?
4) Proposed next meeting to review full results: Tue, Jul 27 at 10am PT. Does that work?

Attached: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_ab_results.csv, ab_test_charts.png

Thanks all — excited about the momentum.

Marissa Cole
